title: "Benchmark of the robust linear regression learner"

---

This vignette compares `LearnerRegrRlm` with three other learners,
using 5-fold cross-validation on two regression data sets.

```{r}
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
lgr::get_logger("mlr3")$set_threshold("warn")
lgr::get_logger("bbotk")$set_threshold("warn")
set.seed(1)
```

## Data sets

We use two regression data sets included with R:
`Boston` from the `MASS` package (median house value),
and `airquality` (ozone concentration), keeping only the rows
without missing values.

```{r}
boston <- mlr3::as_task_regr(MASS::Boston, target = "medv", id = "Boston")
air_dt <- na.omit(data.table(datasets::airquality))
air <- mlr3::as_task_regr(air_dt, target = "Ozone", id = "airquality")
task.list <- list(boston, air)
```

## Learners

```{r}
kknn <- mlr3learners::LearnerRegrKKNN$new()
kknn$param_set$values$k <- paradox::to_tune(1, 30)
learner.list <- list(
  mlr3rlm::LearnerRegrRlm$new(),
  mlr3::LearnerRegrFeatureless$new(),
  mlr3learners::LearnerRegrCVGlmnet$new(),
  mlr3tuning::auto_tuner(
    learner = kknn,
    tuner = mlr3tuning::tnr("grid_search", resolution = 30),
    resampling = mlr3::rsmp("cv", folds = 3),
    measure = mlr3::msr("regr.mse"),
    id = "kknn"))
```

## Benchmark

```{r}
kfoldcv <- mlr3::rsmp("cv", folds = 5)
bench.grid <- mlr3::benchmark_grid(task.list, learner.list, kfoldcv)
bench.result <- mlr3::benchmark(bench.grid)
score_dt <- bench.result$score(mlr3::msr("regr.mse"))
dcast(
  score_dt,
  task_id + learner_id ~ .,
  list(mean, sd),
  value.var = "regr.mse")
```

```{r, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 3}
ggplot()+
  geom_point(aes(
    regr.mse, learner_id),
    shape = 1,
    data = score_dt)+
  facet_grid(. ~ task_id, scales = "free_x")+
  scale_x_log10("Mean squared error on test set (one point per fold)")+
  scale_y_discrete("Learner")
```

## Conclusions
`regr.rlm` is much more accurate than `featureless` in both data sets,
and has accuracy similar to `cv_glmnet` and `kknn`.
